12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
13	
14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
16	
17	## Contents
18	
19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
25	  quasi-finite one.
26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
33	  docstring for the proof route.

44	/-- **Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form**: a locally quasi-finite morphism `π` such
45	that `π ≫ g` is proper and `g` is separated is finite. (Properness of `π` follows by
46	cancellation, and a proper locally quasi-finite morphism is finite.) -/

48	    (π : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyQuasiFinite π] [IsSeparated g] [IsProper (π ≫ g)] :
49	    IsFinite π :=
50	  have : IsProper π := IsProper.of_comp π g

101	4. conclude with `exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` (Zariski's main theorem). -/

119	theorem isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen [IsAffineHom π] (i : Fin 2) :
120	    IsAffineOpen (π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k i) :=

126	  refine le_antisymm le_top fun x _ => ?_
127	  have h : π.base x ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ⊔ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
128	    rw [P1.chartOpen_sup]
129	    trivial

136	theorem finite_app_chartOpen [IsFinite π] (i : Fin 2) :
137	    RingHom.Finite (π.app (P1.chartOpen k i)).hom :=
138	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_chartOpen k i)

145	      (X 0 * X 1))).hom :=
146	  π.finite_app _ (P1.isAffineOpen_overlap k)

8	/-!
9	# Base change of sections along the projection `C ⊗ Spec A ⟶ C`
10	
11	For an object `C` of `Over (Spec k)` (`k` a field), a commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and a
12	quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ C.left`, this file identifies the sections of the
13	base change `(C ⊗ Spec A).left` over the preimage `V_A := (fst C (Spec A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V` of
14	`V` under the first projection with the tensor product of the sections over `V`:
15	
16	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, V_A)`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`), sending `s ⊗ a` to the product of the two
19	pullbacks (`sectionsBaseChange_tmul`), compatibly with restriction along `W ≤ V`
20	(`sectionsBaseChange_naturality`). Here `C ⊗ T` is the cartesian-monoidal product of
21	`Over (Spec k)`, realized by `Limits.pullback`; the single bridge lemma between the two
22	languages is `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`.
23	
24	This is brick 1 of the separatedness ledger (design §4.4): one brick, three consumers —
25	étale separatedness (arbitrary `A`), the dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and the
26	χ-ledger under field extension (`A = K`). Hence the statements are for an arbitrary
27	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and `V` is allowed to be any quasi-compact quasi-separated
28	open (e.g. the intersection of two affines of the curve), not just an affine one.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left` — the bridge: for `X T : Over S`, the scheme-level
33	  square `(fst X T).left, (snd X T).left, X.hom, T.hom` is a pullback.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A` — `Spec A` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`, together with
35	  the instance `Flat (overSpec k A).hom` (automatic over a field).
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` by
37	  restriction of scalars along the structure morphism. Deliberately **not** a global instance
38	  (house rule, cf. `Scheme.overModule`); consumers activate it with
39	  `attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.resAlgHom` — restriction of sections as a `k`-algebra homomorphism.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections_of_isAffineOpen`,
42	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections` — the master pushout squares on sections, for
43	  an arbitrary test object `T` with `T.left` affine (affine `V` needs no flatness; qcqs `V`
44	  needs `[Flat T.hom]`).
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections` — the same square with the
46	  `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)`/`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` corners replaced by `k` and `A`.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`
48	  — the comparison isomorphism (in `CommRingCat`, resp. as a ring equivalence), with the
49	  computation rules `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one`, `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`,
50	  `sectionsBaseChange_tmul` and the restriction-naturality
51	  `sectionsBaseChange_naturality`.
52	
53	## Implementation notes
54	
55	The heavy lifting is mathlib's `pushoutSection` API
56	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Flat.lean`): for a pullback square of schemes the
57	canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, ...)` is an isomorphism for
58	affine `Uₛ, Uₜ` and qcqs `Uₓ` when `T ⟶ S` is flat — which over a field is automatic.
59	This file only supplies the Over-category bridge, the corner bookkeeping (`ΓSpecIso`), and
60	the tensor-product face.
61	
62	The `k`-linear faces consumers may need are one line away from `sectionsBaseChange`:
63	it is `k`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one` applied to
64	`algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V) r` (both sides land in the structure-map image), and
65	`A`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`.
66	-/

342	        (homOfLE (show (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤

348	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
349	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]

351	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, Over.resAlgHom_apply,

354	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,

323	  le_right : U₀₁ ≤ U₁

329	  sup_eq_top : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤

331	  Γ₀ : Γ(P1 k, U₀) ≃+* Polynomial k

335	  Γ₀₁ : Γ(P1 k, U₀₁) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial k

9	/-!
10	# Separatedness brick 3: pullback along the projection is injective on Picard groups
11	
12	For `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and geometrically reduced over a field `k` and
13	**any** test object `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech Picard classes along the second
14	projection `pr : (C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective
15	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.prPullback_injective`) — brick 3 of the separatedness ledger
16	(design §4.4), the cocycle recast of "a line bundle pulled back from the base which
17	trivializes on the product was trivial", the projection step of Kleiman,
18	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1).
19	
20	## The section-level engine
21	
22	Everything reduces to the section rings: for an **affine** open `V ⊆ T.left`, pullback of
23	sections along the projection is bijective,
24	`Γ(T.left, V) ≅ Γ((C ⊗ T).left, pr⁻¹ V)` (`Over.isIso_appLE_snd`). This is brick 2
25	(`Over.isIso_appTop_snd_overSpec`, `Picard/UniversalSections.lean`) freed from its
26	`T = Spec A`, `V = ⊤` special case: the qcqs pushout square of
27	`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Flat` is applied to the pullback square
28	`(C ⊗ T).left = C.left ×_{Spec k} T.left` with the *affine* slot at `V ⊆ T.left` and the
29	*qcqs* slot at `⊤ ⊆ C.left`, and the `k ≅ Γ(C.left, 𝒪)` leg (Wave 1) transfers the
30	isomorphism across the square. Flatness of `T.hom` is automatic over a field
31	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.of_field`). By sheaf separation the injectivity half extends to
32	**arbitrary** opens `W ⊆ T.left` (`Over.appLE_snd_injective`), which is why no affineness
33	or quasi-separatedness hypothesis on `T` survives into the final statement.
34	
35	## The cocycle assembly
36	
37	A Picard class on `T` dying on `C ⊗ T` is represented, after refining to an affine
38	pointed cover `𝒰` (`Scheme.PointedCover.exists_isAffineOpen_le`), by a unit cocycle `γ`
39	whose pullback is — by refinement injectivity, `Picard/RefinementInjectivity.lean` — a
40	coboundary `w` **on the pulled-back cover itself**. Choosing a point `sec t` in each
41	fiber of the (surjective) projection, the trivializing units `w (sec t) ∈ 𝒪ˣ(pr⁻¹ 𝒰 t)`
42	descend through the section bijection (`Over.unitsAppLE_snd_bijective`) to units
43	`v t ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰 t)`, and the coboundary relation for `v` follows from the one for `w` by
44	injectivity of pullback on `𝒰 t ⊓ 𝒰 t'`.
45	-/

197	/-- The projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is surjective: `C.hom` is surjective (its

202	    inferInstance

204	/-- The descent step for `prPullback_injective`, with the fiber points and the descended
205	units abstracted: if the pullback cocycle of `γ` is the coboundary of `w`, and `vt, vt'`
206	pull back to the trivializing units of `w` at points `z, z'` of the product lying over
207	`t, t'`, then `vt, vt'` satisfy the coboundary relation for `γ` at `(t, t')`. The
208	equations `hz, hz'` let the fiber-point choices be substituted away. -/
209	private lemma descend_coboundary {𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover}
210	    (γ : T.left.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
211	    (w : ∀ z : (C ⊗ T).left,
212	      Γ((C ⊗ T).left, (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)ˣ)
213	    (hw : ∀ z z',
214	      (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
215	          (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
216	              ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
217	            ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
218	          * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
219	        = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z'))
220	    (z z' : (C ⊗ T).left) (t t' : T.left)
221	    (hz : (snd C T).left.base z = t) (hz' : (snd C T).left.base z' = t')
222	    (hzle : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z)
223	    (hz'le : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')
224	    (vt : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ) (vt' : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t')ˣ)
225	    (hvt : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t)
226	        le_rfl vt = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hzle (w z))
227	    (hvt' : (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t') ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t')
228	        le_rfl vt' = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict hz'le (w z')) :
229	    T.left.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens t ⊓ 𝒰.opens t' ≤ 𝒰.opens t) vt
230	        * Scheme.unitsEvInf γ t t'
231	      = T.left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right vt' := by
232	  subst hz hz'
233	  -- apply injectivity of pullback of unit sections on `𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z')`
234	  have hinj : Function.Injective ((snd C T).left.unitsAppLE
235	      (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
236	      ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
237	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z')))
238	      le_rfl) :=
239	    fun a b hab ↦ Units.ext (appLE_snd_injective C T _ (congrArg Units.val hab))
240	  apply hinj
241	  rw [map_mul]
242	  -- the descended units, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
243	  have e₁ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
244	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.1 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
245	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
246	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z))) hvt
247	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₁
248	  have e₂ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
249	    (fun y hy ↦ hy.2 : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
250	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
251	      ≤ (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))) hvt'
252	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict] at e₂
253	  -- the coboundary relation for `w`, restricted to `pr⁻¹(𝒰 (pr z) ⊓ 𝒰 (pr z'))`
254	  have e₃ := congrArg ((C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
255	    (fun y hy ↦ ⟨hy.1, hy.2⟩ : (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ
256	        (𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z) ⊓ 𝒰.opens ((snd C T).left.base z'))
257	      ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
258	          ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z')) (hw z z')
259	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict, Scheme.unitsRestrict_unitsRestrict,
260	    Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map] at e₃
261	  -- assemble
262	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, e₁, e₂]
263	  exact e₃
264	
265	/-- **Brick 3 of the separatedness ledger** (design §4.4; the projection step of Kleiman,
266	*The Picard Scheme*, Theorem 2.5(1)): for `C` proper, geometrically irreducible and
267	geometrically reduced over the field `k` and **any** `T` over `Spec k`, pullback of Čech
268	Picard classes along the second projection `(C ⊗ T).left ⟶ T.left` is injective. -/
269	theorem prPullback_injective :
270	    Function.Injective (Scheme.CechPic.map (X := (C ⊗ T).left) (snd C T).left) := by
271	  -- the `H¹`-level heart, on an affine pointed cover
272	  have H : ∀ (𝒰 : T.left.PointedCover), (∀ t, IsAffineOpen (𝒰.opens t)) →
273	      ∀ a : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰, (snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a = 1 → a = 1 := by
274	    intro 𝒰 haff a ha
275	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
276	    replace ha : ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).class = OneCocycle.class 1 := ha
277	    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ :=
278	      (OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mp ((OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mp ha)
279	    -- the coboundary data, in `Γ`-typed form
280	    have hw' : ∀ z z',
281	        (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
282	            (inf_le_left : (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z
283	                ⊓ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z'
284	              ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens z) (w z)
285	            * Scheme.unitsEvInf ((snd C T).left.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) z z'
286	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict inf_le_right (w z') := by
287	      intro z z'
288	      have h1 := hw z z'
289	      rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul] at h1
290	      exact h1
291	    -- choose a point in each fiber of the projection, descend the trivializing units
292	    obtain ⟨sec, hsec⟩ := (snd C T).left.surjective.hasRightInverse
293	    have hchoice : ∀ t, ∃ v : Γ(T.left, 𝒰.opens t)ˣ,
294	        (snd C T).left.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens t) ((snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t) le_rfl v
295	          = (C ⊗ T).left.unitsRestrict
296	              (le_of_eq (by rw [Scheme.PointedCover.pullback_opens, hsec t]) :
297	                (snd C T).left ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens t
298	                  ≤ (𝒰.pullback (snd C T).left).opens (sec t)) (w (sec t)) :=
299	      fun t ↦ (unitsAppLE_snd_bijective C T (haff t)).surjective _
300	    choose v hv using hchoice
301	    -- the descended units witness the coboundary relation for `γ`
302	    rw [show (1 : T.left.unitsH1 𝒰) = OneCocycle.class 1 from rfl]
303	    refine (OneCocycle.class_eq_iff _ _).mpr
304	      ((OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf _ _).mpr ⟨v, fun t t' ↦ ?_⟩)
305	    rw [OneCocycle.one_evInf, one_mul]
306	    exact descend_coboundary C T γ w hw' (sec t) (sec t') t t' (hsec t) (hsec t')
307	      _ _ (v t) (v t') (hv t) (hv t')
308	  -- assembly: refine to an affine pointed cover and use `CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff`
309	  refine (injective_iff_map_eq_one _).mpr fun x hx ↦ ?_
310	  induction x using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰₀ a₀ =>
311	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle, haff⟩ := 𝒰₀.exists_isAffineOpen_le
312	  rw [← Scheme.CechPic.mk_unitsRes hle] at hx ⊢
313	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.map_mk, Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff] at hx
314	  rw [Scheme.CechPic.mk_eq_one_iff]
315	  exact H 𝒰 haff _ hx

9	# The projective line over a field, with usable charts
10	
11	We define `AlgebraicGeometry.P1 k` as `Proj` of the standard graded polynomial ring
12	`k[X₀, X₁]` (`MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k` with the degree grading), together with:
13	
14	* `P1.structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k)`, and the instance `IsProper (P1.structureMap k)`
15	  (inherited from mathlib's properness of `Proj`);
16	* the two standard affine charts `D₊(X₀)`, `D₊(X₁)` (`P1.chartOpen`), which cover `P1 k`
17	  (`P1.chartOpen_sup`), together with the open immersions `P1.chartι i` from the affine
18	  models `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`;
19	* identifications of the chart section rings with polynomial rings:
20	  `P1.awayAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[t]` (the coordinate is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`).
21	
22	The identification of the chart *overlap* with Laurent polynomials, the section-level
23	versions, and the bundled chart package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` are in the
24	continuation file `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts`.
25	
26	The generic instance `Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x)` (for a graded `R`-algebra) and
27	the lemma `LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval` (*Laurent span*: every Laurent
28	polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a polynomial in `T⁻¹`) are general-purpose
29	and live in their natural namespaces.
30	
31	## Implementation notes
32	
33	We install `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a (project-global) instance: everywhere in this
34	project, `MvPolynomial` carries the standard degree grading. Mathlib leaves this to the user
35	because other gradings exist; this project only ever uses the standard one.
36	-/

388	    rw [map_pow, polyToAway_X]

9	/-!
10	# The Picard class of a unit Čech cocycle on an affine scheme
11	
12	For an affine scheme `X`, a unit Čech cocycle `γ` on a pointed cover `𝒰` determines a
13	class in mathlib's Picard group `CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`, by faithfully flat descent along
14	a finite basic refinement of `𝒰`:
15	
16	* `Scheme.PointedCover.BasicRefinement`: finitely many points `pt i` and sections
17	  `r i : Γ(X, ⊤)` with `X.basicOpen (r i) ≤ 𝒰.opens (pt i)`, covering `X`.  Such data
18	  always exists (`BasicRefinement.nonempty`): basic opens form a basis of an affine
19	  scheme, which is quasi-compact.
20	* `BasicRefinement.coverCocycle γ`: the evaluations `γ (pt i, pt j)` restricted to the
21	  pairwise overlaps `X.basicOpen (r i * r j)` — a Čech cocycle of units on the finite
22	  localization cover `r` in the sense of `IsLocalization.AwayCover.IsCoverCocycle`
23	  (`BasicRefinement.isCoverCocycle`; the canonical algebra maps between localizations
24	  agree with restriction of sections by uniqueness, `Scheme.basicOpen_algHom_ext`).
25	* `BasicRefinement.pic γ : CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`: the Picard class of the invertible
26	  module descended from the associated descent 1-cocycle
27	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.UnitDescent`) along the faithfully flat cover algebra
28	  `∀ i, Γ(X, X.basicOpen (r i))`.
29	
30	The independence of `pic γ` from all choices, and the resulting group homomorphism
31	`X.CechPic →* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤)`, are established in
32	`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicAffine`.
33	-/

48	/-! ## Basic refinements of a pointed cover -/
49	
50	/-- A finite basic refinement of a pointed cover of a scheme: finitely many points and
51	sections whose basic opens refine the cover at those points and still cover `X`.  The
52	index type is a field, so that refinements can be merged (`BasicRefinement.inter`). -/
53	structure PointedCover.BasicRefinement (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type (u + 1) where
54	  /-- The index type of the refinement. -/
55	  ι : Type u
56	  /-- The index type is finite. -/
57	  [fintype : Fintype ι]
58	  /-- The index type has decidable equality. -/
59	  [decEq : DecidableEq ι]
60	  /-- The chosen points. -/
61	  pt : ι → X
62	  /-- The sections cutting out the basic opens. -/
63	  r : ι → Γ(X, ⊤)
64	  /-- Each basic open refines the cover at its point. -/
65	  basicOpen_le : ∀ i, X.basicOpen (r i) ≤ 𝒰.opens (pt i)
66	  /-- The basic opens cover `X`. -/
67	  iSup_eq : (⨆ i, X.basicOpen (r i)) = ⊤

73	/-- Every pointed cover of an affine scheme admits a finite basic refinement: basic
74	opens form a basis and the space is quasi-compact. -/
75	theorem nonempty [IsAffine X] (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Nonempty 𝒰.BasicRefinement := by
76	  have hex : ∀ x : X, ∃ f : Γ(X, ⊤), X.basicOpen f ≤ 𝒰.opens x ∧ x ∈ X.basicOpen f :=
77	    fun x ↦ (isAffineOpen_top X).exists_basicOpen_le
78	      (⟨x, 𝒰.mem_opens x⟩ : (𝒰.opens x : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)) trivial
79	  choose f hf₁ hf₂ using hex
80	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover isCompact_univ
81	    (fun x : X ↦ (X.basicOpen (f x) : Set X)) (fun x ↦ (X.basicOpen (f x)).isOpen)
82	    (fun x _ ↦ Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨x, hf₂ x⟩)
83	  letI : DecidableEq X := Classical.decEq X
84	  refine ⟨{ ι := ↥t, pt := fun y ↦ (y : X), r := fun y ↦ f (y : X),
85	            basicOpen_le := fun y ↦ hf₁ _, iSup_eq := ?_ }⟩
86	  rw [eq_top_iff]
87	  intro x _
88	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp (ht (Set.mem_univ x))
89	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨⟨y, hy.1⟩, hy.2⟩
90	
91	/-- Merging two basic refinements: the products of the sections, indexed by pairs, with
92	the points of the **second** refinement.  The result refines every pointed cover that the
93	second refinement refines. -/
94	@[simps]
95	def inter {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (P : 𝒰.BasicRefinement) (Q : 𝒱.BasicRefinement) :
96	    𝒱.BasicRefinement where
97	  ι := P.ι × Q.ι
98	  pt p := Q.pt p.2
99	  r p := P.r p.1 * Q.r p.2
100	  basicOpen_le p := ((X.basicOpen_mul _ _).trans_le inf_le_right).trans (Q.basicOpen_le p.2)
101	  iSup_eq := by
102	    rw [eq_top_iff]
103	    intro x _
104	    have hxP : x ∈ ⨆ i, X.basicOpen (P.r i) := P.iSup_eq.ge trivial
105	    have hxQ : x ∈ ⨆ j, X.basicOpen (Q.r j) := Q.iSup_eq.ge trivial

10	# The two-affine-cover H¹ cokernel bridge
11	
12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` covered by two affine opens `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, this file
13	computes the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf (as a sheaf of `k`-modules on
14	the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) as an explicit cokernel of a map of section
15	modules:
16	
17	`H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪ₖ) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁) ⧸ range((s₀, s₁) ↦ s₀|_{U₀⊓U₁} - s₁|_{U₀⊓U₁})`
18	
19	(`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`, with the cokernel carrier
20	`AlgebraicGeometry.TwoCover.H1Cok`). This is the computational access point for the genus
21	of a curve: `genus C = finrank k H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C)` becomes the corank of an explicit map of
22	function spaces.
23	
24	**Hypotheses actually used**: `X` any scheme over `Spec k`, `IsAffineOpen U₀`,
25	`IsAffineOpen U₁`, `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`. In particular *no* affineness (or even
26	quasi-compactness) hypothesis on the intersection `U₀ ⊓ U₁` is needed — unlike for the
27	classical Čech-complex identification, the derived-functor Mayer–Vietoris sequence of
28	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.MayerVietoris` is exact regardless, and affineness of the
29	two pieces alone kills their `H¹'` (`IsAffineOpen.subsingleton_moduleKSheaf_hModule'_one`).

32	
33	* `Scheme.twoCoverSquare` — the Mayer–Vietoris square `(U₀ ⊓ U₁, U₀, U₁, ⊤)` on the
34	  small Zariski site of `X`, for a covering pair of opens.

36	  `k`-modules with `H¹'(U₀, F)` and `H¹'(U₁, F)` subsingletons,

38	* `TwoCover.diff k X U₀ U₁` — the difference map `Γ(U₀) × Γ(U₁) →ₗ[k] Γ(U₀ ⊓ U₁)`.

# Finiteness of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)` via a finite morphism to the projective line

For a scheme `X` over `Spec k` equipped with a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`, this
file proves that the degree-one cohomology of the structure sheaf of `X` (as a sheaf of
`k`-modules on the small Zariski site, `Sheaf.HModule`) is a finite `k`-module — and derives
the instance for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve of the challenge, so that
`genus` is the dimension of an honestly finite-dimensional vector space.

The proof is the *two-lattice ladder* of `AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.TwoLattice` run on the
Mayer–Vietoris cokernel of `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.TwoCover`:

* `V i := π ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` is an affine open cover of `X`
  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), so
  `H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁) ⧸ range (res₀ - res₁)` (`TwoCover.h1CokEquiv`);
* `N := Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)` is a module over the Laurent polynomial ring `k[T;T⁻¹]` through
  `π`'s map on sections over the chart overlap and the identification
  `Γ(ℙ¹, D₊(X₀X₁)) ≃ k[T,T⁻¹]` (`P1.overlapSectionsEquiv`); it is module-finite because `π`
  is finite (`finite_app_overlap`);
* `Q₀, Q₁ :=` the images of `Γ(V₀), Γ(V₁)` in `N` are `k`-submodules with
  `range (res₀ - res₁) = Q₀ ⊔ Q₁`; `Q₀` is stable under `T` because `T` is the restriction
  of the chart-0 coordinate, which extends to `V₀` (symmetrically for `Q₁` and `T⁻¹`); and
  `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is the basic open of the pulled-back chart coordinate inside the affine `V₀`
  (`P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`), so
  `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_of_eq_basicOpen` provides the surjectivity-up-to-powers
  hypotheses of the two-lattice lemma.

The `ℙ¹`-side identifications live in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.FinitenessP1`.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1` — **the conditional
  finiteness theorem**: if `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹` is finite with `π ≫ P1.structureMap k = X ↘ Spec k`,
  then `Module.Finite k (H¹ₖ(X, 𝒪_X))`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_one` — the instance for the challenge curve
  `C` (smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible over `k`), consuming
  `exists_isFinite_toP1`; it is keyed on exactly the `letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k))`
  spelling used by `genus` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Challenge`.

`FiniteDimensional k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` is *definitionally* the statement of the instance
(`FiniteDimensional` is an abbreviation for `Module.Finite`), so no separate corollary is
needed.
-/
